thread.title: Apple: Doubling Of Services Revenue To $100 Billion - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Bluesea Research
title: Apple: Doubling Of Services Revenue To $100 Billion - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
A recent report estimates that Apple ( AAPL ) could hit a revenue target of $100 billion in Services segment by 2023. Apple has reported $37 billion revenue in this segment in FY18. Tim Cook had set a target of doubling Services revenue from 2016 base by end of 2020. Apple will most likely r each this target sooner than estimated. The management can then announce another target to double the Services revenue to over $100 billion within a 3 to 4 years time frame.
In this report, Morgan Stanley analyst Katy Huberty has projected that Apple could show massive growth in Services. This should be bullish for the stock considering that Apple’s management will stop giving unit sales data and is trying to move Wall Street’s focus to Services instead of products. She also points that much of the incremental gross profit growth will come from Services segment. However, Apple faces massive challenges in several verticals within the Services segment. In these vertical Apple would need to deliver margins and growth better than the competition to build a long-term growth momentum in the stock.
Is it too soon to talk about $100 billion Services target? The article linked above was published on 15th October in which I mentioned, “If Apple hits the target of $50 billion by 2020, it could set an even bigger goal of doubling the revenue from Services segment in another 5-7 years.” Katy Huberty’s report published in mid-November has the same estimates in which she forecasts Apple to hit $100 billion Services revenue by 2023. Apple’s management has already made it clear that they see the future of the company totally dependent on Services segment. Currently, Services segment makes only 14% of the total revenue base. As Apple diverts more resources to streaming content and new services, we should see the revenue share of this segment increase significantly.
Source: Morgan Stanley Research
The revenue growth needs to translate to better profit growth. The report also shows a better profit trajectory in the next few years as Services forms a larger share of the incremental profit. We can see from the above chart that Apple’s incremental profit from 2012 to 2018 has seen massive swings. However, from 2019 onwards, the profit growth becomes a lot more stable. A large part of this growth is due to Services segment which is estimated to have only $0.63 of incremental gross profit in 2018 but will have $1.72 incremental EPS share by 2022.
It is difficult to imagine that in the near future Wall Street will move away from the focus on unit sales and revenue growth of iPhone segment. But over time, as the revenue share of Services increases, we should see individual verticals within Services gain greater importance. In the last earnings call, the management has also mentioned that they will report costs and margins of different verticals within the Services segment.
Growth in user base We know that Apple’s unit sales have stagnated for a long time. However, the overall user base of the company is still growing at a healthy pace. Tim Cook mentioned in the earnings that the company is seeing double-digit growth within installed base. This is reflected in the recent CIRP report which shows US installed base growing to over 180 million from less than 160 million in the year-ago period.
Source: CIRP
One of the reasons behind stagnant unit sales and growth in installed base is that Apple devices enjoy a good resale value . Hence, the overall usage of the device increases substantially even if the new purchases are lower. Apple should be able to use this positive tailwind to build better Services growth and create a tighter ecosystem.
Stumbling blocks The growth in Services segment is not without its share of challenges. I believe some of the verticals targeted by Apple are heavily platform agnostic. This means that choosing Apple’s service over a competitor does not improve the user experience significantly. Within these services, it is also difficult to leverage the brand equity of the company to extract a premium price.
The best example of this is Apple Music. Apple has been trying to attract more users to its Music service but Spotify ( SPOT ) has shown a strong challenge. The pricing of both the services is exactly the same. Even if Apple gains an upper hand in terms of total subscribers, it is unlikely that it will be able to get a premium over its competitor. If Apple charges 20% or 30% premium for Apple Music, customers could easily move to Spotify. An estimate in WSJ shows that Apple Music has a gross margin of 15% whereas SPOT has gross margin of 26%.
Apple will also face challenge in the cloud service from Alphabet ( GOOG ). In China, Apple faces challenge from Alibaba ( BABA ) and Tencent. Both these giants have created huge ecosystems where customers can get almost any service they need. We can already see this from the poor growth of Apple Pay in China. Apple has started accepting Alibaba’s Alipay in its retail stores for the convenience of its customers.
Alibaba and Tencent have cornered overwhelming market share within digital payment service of China. Hence, it is difficult for Apple users to move to Apple Pay without seeing significant friction in the services they can access. Alibaba and companies backed by it have shown good growth in digital services in emerging economies of Southeast Asia and South Asia. Apple is targeting these regions to increase its target audience base.
If Apple is able to overcome these challenges and deliver strong growth within important verticals of Services segment, we should see better growth potential for the company.
Investor Takeaway Apple could hit $100 billion in Services segment by 2023 according to recent estimates by Morgan Stanley. Continuous growth within this segment should be a big positive for the company. It will also stabilize the future EPS growth, improving the valuation multiple for the company. Increase in user base will also help the company target a larger audience base for its services.
However, Apple faces a number of challenges within this segment. Some of the verticals are platform agnostic which reduces the ability to gain premium pricing. Apple will also face significant challenges from big tech giants like Amazon ( AMZN ), Alphabet, Alibaba and Tencent. This can lead to erosion of margin. Investors need to look at the margin trajectory of individual verticals of Services segment to gauge the future potential of the stock.
